title: Define required statistical breakdowns beyond simple aggregates
when_to_use: When the task requests analyzing bottlenecks, drop-offs, or efficiency of a process.
experience:
- Before reporting final results, explicitly list all metrics and dimensions required by the task or rubric.
- For each reported aggregate (e.g., average days, attrition rate), plan to compute supporting statistics (e.g., counts of progressed vs. attrited, pass rates, stage-to-hire conversion).
- Ensure analysis includes both progression-based and attribution-based perspectives if applicable (e.g., compute both counts of candidates who advanced and counts for each attrition reason).
- Validate that your computed metrics match anchor points or expected ranges provided in the rubric.
- If analyzing time-based bottlenecks, also compute percentiles and time-bin attrition rates to detect long-tail delays.
checklist: Identify required supporting statistics beyond main metrics
Compute both progression and attribution perspectives
common_failure_prevented: Reports only aggregated attrition rates without supporting progression counts or stage-to-hire conversion, leading to incomplete bottleneck analysis.

title: Analyze time-spent structure beyond the average
when_to_use: When evaluating process duration or identifying time-related bottlenecks.
experience:
- Do not rely solely on average days; compute percentiles (e.g., 75th, 90th) to understand spread.
- Segment average days by outcome (e.g., avg days for progressed vs. attrited candidates).
- Create time bins (e.g., <10 days, 10–25 days, >25 days) and calculate attrition/pass rates per bin.
- Report the proportion of candidates in the long tail (e.g., exceeding a threshold).
- Use this detailed structure to pinpoint whether long delays are correlated with attrition.
checklist: Segment average days by outcome groups
Calculate attrition rates per time bin
common_failure_prevented: Only reports average time spent, missing insights into long-tail delays and their correlation with attrition.

title: Establish a clear business-stage order before funnel analysis
when_to_use: When analyzing a multi-stage funnel or pipeline with sequential steps.
experience:
- Before computing stage metrics, determine the correct sequential order of stages (e.g., from application to hire).
- Use business logic, stage IDs, or timestamp patterns to define a mapping (e.g., assign ranks 1 to N).
- Validate the order by checking median timestamps or known business flow.
- If using raw records, explicitly note the risk of timestamp reversals (e.g., due to data corrections) and how your mapping mitigates it.
- Report the defined stage order as part of the methodology.
checklist: Map each stage to a rank
Validate order with timestamps or business logic
common_failure_prevented: Analyzes stages without establishing their logical sequence, undermining funnel progression analysis.
